text: The Patriots suffered a 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday night in Chicago, with Caleb Williams throwing two touchdown passes to lead the upset, and the loss has only underscored one of Mike Vrabel's four pillars of team identity: turnover differential, an area where New England is visibly struggling. The offensive line took a hit heading into the game with starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown both ruled out due to injuries, and while film review of Drake Maye's performance and the defense's breakdowns will occupy the analysts this week, there were some bright spots—notably Rhamondre Stevenson reaching a career high in receiving yards and continuing his run of excellence doing the little things that keep drives alive. With Stevenson now on the cusp of 100 carries for his sixth straight season, the Patriots appear to have at least one weapon executing at a high level, though the turnover battle and the defensive vulnerabilities exposed by Williams and company suggest deeper structural problems that need addressing before Round 3 against these Bears.
